title: Statistics: Bar Graphs, Histograms and Frequency Polygons
seo_title: Statistics Class 9 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)
standard_text: Bar graphs, histograms (with varying base lengths) and frequency polygons (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Statistics worksheet (NCERT Chapter 12): reading bar graphs, histograms with equal and varying class widths, class marks and frequency polygons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Histogram heights: frequency ÷ width × minimum width
key_sub: Frequency polygon: plot (class mark, frequency) and close it at both ends.
body_html:
How it works

A bar graph uses bars of equal width with gaps between them. A histogram shows grouped data: the bars stand on the classes, with no gaps.

If the class widths are different, the bar heights must be adjusted: adjusted frequency = frequency ÷ class width × minimum class size. Then the areas match the frequencies.

For a frequency polygon, plot (class mark, frequency) for each class and join the points. Close it on the x-axis at the class marks of an imaginary class before the first and after the last.

Example

The class 20–40 has frequency 12 and the minimum class size is 10. Find the height of its bar.

12 ÷ 20 × 10

Answer: 6

Example

Which point is plotted for the class 30–40 with frequency 7?

Class mark = (30 + 40) ÷ 2 = 35

Answer: (35, 7)

Common mistakes

  • Drawing bars for unequal classes with the frequency as the height.
  • Plotting the upper limit of a class instead of its class mark.
  • Counting a value of 40 in the class 30–40. With exclusive classes it belongs to 40–50.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bar graph and a histogram?
faq.a: A bar graph shows separate categories with gaps between bars. A histogram shows continuous grouped data, with bars standing on the classes and no gaps.

faq.q: How do you draw a histogram with varying class widths?
faq.a: Use the minimum class size and find each adjusted frequency = frequency ÷ class width × minimum class size. Use these as the heights.
The mid-point of a class: (lower limit + upper limit) ÷ 2.

faq.q: How do you draw a frequency polygon?
faq.a: Plot (class mark, frequency) for every class, join the points with straight lines and close the polygon at the class marks of imaginary classes of frequency zero at each end.
